content.text:
Both plans written and queued as **#12a** and **#12b**. Also: **PR #30's CI passed** — `verify` green in 1m32s, mergeable.

## The wear-confirmation plan (#12a)

Buildable now, no push needed. But it has **a dependency neither of us had spotted**: nothing in the app records that a look was *opened*. `outfits` has no `viewed_at` and nothing writes one — so the rule you set ("it asks only about looks actually opened") can't be implemented without adding it. That's the plan's one schema change, and it comes with a trap: the write must happen from the client on mount, **not** in the Server Component's render, or it fires for prefetches the user never sees.

Both of your rules are encoded as tests rather than prose — Yes/No must have identical styling, and there's a test asserting no dismiss/close/skip control exists at all, because that's the lone-Yes problem wearing a different hat.

**One question I left open rather than deciding:** what a backdrop tap does. My recommendation is that it closes for the session *without* setting `askedOn`, so a mis-tap doesn't silently consume the day's question.

## The notifications plan (#12b)

Two things you should know before this ever gets scheduled.

**The design promises more than a reminder.** `Fitcheck.dc.html:1383` reads *"Tomorrow's weather + a planned look"* — a *planned look* means generating an outfit per subscriber per night, pushed rather than pulled. That's roughly **$90/month per 1000 subscribed users**, against **~$0** for weather alone. It also pre-commits the stylist before the user has said what the day is, which the smart-default work treats as a prediction on purpose. I recommend weather-only and flagged it as **blocking** — it's your money and your product call, not the implementer's.

**iOS is the harder constraint.** Push reaches only home-screen-installed PWAs. Most of your users are iPhone users in a Safari tab, and for them nothing will ever arrive. The plan makes the toggle explain installing rather than render a switch that's on and silent — which is exactly why it was cut from Settings rather than shipped inert.

Two smaller things it pins: the cron route must authenticate (`CRON_SECRET`), because an open one is a public endpoint that pushes to your whole userbase; and it's the first server-side code to run as service role, where RLS doesn't protect you and every query has to scope `user_id` itself.

Also left open: whether the reminder hour is user-chosen, and whether this is free or Pro — `MONETISATION.md` doesn't tier it, though free is the consistent answer since it drives the habit loop that §3 says creates a payer.

**PR #30 is ready to merge whenever you are.**
so with reminder makes no sense to make, only if we will do ios app later

Agreed — with one refinement worth pinning down, because it changes *when* this unblocks.

**It isn't gated on a native iOS app.** Web push works on iOS 16.4+ for PWAs installed to the home screen, and Fitcheck is a PWA from day one with `display: standalone` already set. So the real gate is **installs**, not Capacitor. If you later add an install prompt and people actually add it to their home screen, the same plan ships unchanged. A native app would also unblock it, but it's the more expensive route to the same place.

Either way your conclusion holds for now: building a multi-day push stack to reach the small fraction of users who've installed is the wrong order of work. `CLAUDE.md` already defers web-push to Phase 2 and Capacitor to Phase 4+, so this matches the roadmap rather than fighting it.

**I'd park the plan, not delete it** — it holds the research you'd otherwise redo: the VAPID/subscription shape, the DST-safe due calculation, the cron-auth hole, the service-role caveat, and the cost table for the design's "planned look" copy.

# Usage & Pricing for Cron Jobs

> **🔒 Permissions Required**: Cron Jobs

Cron jobs invoke [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions). This means the same [usage](/docs/limits) and [pricing](/pricing) limits will apply.

|                | **Number of cron jobs per project** | **Minimum interval** | **Scheduling precision** |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| **Hobby**      | 100 cron jobs                       | Once per day         | Per-hour (±59 min)       |
| **Pro**        | 100 cron jobs                       | Once per minute      | Per-minute               |
| **Enterprise** | 100 cron jobs                       | Once per minute      | Per-minute               |

### Hobby scheduling limits

> **💡 Note:** Hobby accounts are limited to cron jobs that run **once per day**. Cron
> expressions that would run more frequently will fail during deployment.

Hobby plans have two restrictions on cron jobs:

1. **Daily execution limit**: Cron jobs can only run once per day. Expressions like `0 * * * *` (per-hour) or `*/30 * * * *` (every 30 minutes) will fail deployment with the error:
   *Hobby accounts are limited to daily cron jobs. This cron expression would run more than once per day.*

2. **Timing precision**: Vercel cannot assure a timely cron job invocation. For example, a cron job configured as `0 1 * * *` (every day at 1 am) will trigger anywhere between 1:00 am and 1:59 am.

For cron jobs that run more frequently or with precise timing, **upgrade to our [Pro](/docs/plans/pro-plan) plan**.

## Pricing

Cron jobs are included in **all plans**.

You use a function to invoke a cron job, and therefore [usage](/docs/limits) and [pricing](/pricing) limits for these functions apply to all cron job executions:

- [Functions limits and pricing](/docs/functions/usage-and-pricing)

Verified, and it's a real trap in the plan I just wrote.

## What's free

**The push itself costs nothing.** FCM, APNs and Mozilla's autopush are run by the browser vendors at no charge — there's no per-message fee for web push, at any volume. VAPID keys are self-generated, `web-push` is open source, and the subscriptions table is a rounding error on Supabase.

## What actually costs money

**1. The scheduler — and my plan wouldn't have deployed.** Vercel's docs are explicit:

> **Hobby accounts are limited to cron jobs that run once per day.** Cron expressions that would run more frequently will **fail during deployment.**

My plan specifies `0 * * * *` (hourly), which is exactly the example they give as failing. And Hobby's scheduling precision is **±59 minutes**, so even a daily cron fires anywhere inside an hour — useless for "remind me at 07:00".

Hourly granularity isn't optional here: users are in different timezones, so you need to check every hour who's at their local 7am. That means **Vercel Pro, $20/month**.

**2. Option B's pre-generated looks** — ~$90/month per 1000 subscribers, as before.

## But the $20 is avoidable

The scheduler doesn't have to be Vercel:

- **Supabase `pg_cron` + `pg_net`** — included free, runs on any interval, calls your route handler. You're already on Supabase, and this keeps the trigger next to the data it reads.
- **GitHub Actions on a schedule** — free for public repos, and this repo is public. A 3-line workflow curling the endpoint with the secret.

So the honest total for a weather-only reminder is **€0/month**, provided the cron doesn't run on Vercel Hobby.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p = "docs/MONETISATION.md"
s = open(p).read()

s = s.replace("""## 7. Open questions""",
"""## 7. What a break-even model needs, and what this document was missing

_Added 2026-08-12, when a break-even model was first asked for._

**Sections 1–4 model COST-TO-SERVE, not a business.** They answer "what does an AI generation cost", and
they answer it well and by measurement. A break-even model needs three more things this document did not
have: what actually reaches the bank from €5, the infrastructure that is not AI, and the fixed costs
that exist whether anyone subscribes or not.

### 7.1 €5 is not €5 — roughly €3.84 reaches us

Verified against Stripe's published EEA pricing, 2026-08-12:

| Line | On a €5/mo subscription |
|---|---|
| Gross | €5.00 |
| **VAT** (EU digital services, OSS — 19% DE, 17% LU … 27% HU) | **−€0.80** if the price is VAT-INCLUSIVE |
| **Stripe**, EEA standard card — 1.5% + €0.25 | −€0.33 |
| **Stripe Billing** — 0.7% of volume | −€0.04 |
| **Net** | **≈ €3.84** |

That is a **23% haircut**, and two things inside it deserve attention:

- **The €0.25 fixed fee is 5% on its own at this price**, before any percentage applies. It is the
  single strongest argument for the annual plan §7.2 lists as undecided: at €48/yr the same fixed fee is
  0.5%, and net rises from ~€3.84×12 = €46 to about €51.
- **A premium (rewards/business) card costs 2.8% + €0.25, not 1.5%** — a mix assumption, not a constant.
- ⚠️ **Whether €5 is VAT-inclusive or exclusive is not decided anywhere.** If exclusive, a German
  customer pays €5.95 and roughly €4.58 reaches us. This single unstated choice moves net revenue ~19%.

### 7.2 Infrastructure this document never counted

| Cost | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Open-Meteo** | ⚠️ **LICENSING EXPOSURE** | The free API is **not permitted for commercial use** — verified 2026-08-12. `CLAUDE.md` records it as "free, no key", which was true while nothing was sold. Weather is on the critical path of every generate. A paid tier is required the day Pro is charged for, and CC BY 4.0 attribution is mandatory in the app regardless. |
| **Supabase egress** | **Not counted, likely dominant** | §2 measured STORAGE (330 kB/item) but never bandwidth. Every closet screen, flat-lay and diary cell serves cutouts through signed URLs, so egress scales with *engagement*, not just library size — and egress is the metered line, not gigabytes at rest. **This needs measuring before any model is trusted.** |
| **Supabase plan** | Not counted | Free tier caps DB, storage, egress and MAU; Pro is $25/mo plus usage. |
| **Vercel** | Not counted | ⚠️ Hobby is **non-commercial only**, so a paid product needs Pro at **$20/mo**. That also removes the cron restriction recorded in `plans/scoping/2026-08-11-notifications.md`. |
| **Domain** | Not counted | ~€12/yr. |
| **App store commission** | Not counted, future | If Capacitor ships (Phase 4+), Apple requires In-App Purchase for a digital subscription: **15% under the Small Business Program, otherwise 30%** — replacing Stripe's ~7%, not adding to it. Verify current terms before committing; it changes the price you must charge to net the same. |

### 7.3 The shape of the model

```
Break-even subscribers  =  fixed monthly costs
                           ─────────────────────────────────────────
                           net revenue/Pro − (cost to serve 1 Pro
                                              + free users per Pro
                                                × cost to serve 1 free)
```

Everything on the right except *fixed monthly costs* and *free users per Pro* is measurable today. The
two unmeasured inputs are **Supabase egress per active user** and the **Open-Meteo commercial tier**.

**Worked illustration — not a forecast, and not advice.** Using this document's own measured figures
(free ≈ $0.14/mo AI, Pro ≈ $0.90/mo heavy), €3.84 net, fixed costs of Vercel $20 + Supabase $25 + domain
≈ **$46/mo**, and §2's 5% conversion (so 19 free users per Pro):

```
contribution per Pro ≈ 3.84 − (0.90 + 19 × 0.14) ≈ €0.28
break-even ≈ 46 / 0.28 ≈ 164 Pro subscribers ≈ 3,300 total users
```

⚠️ **That €0.28 is razor-thin and is the real finding.** It is dominated by the *free* users each payer
carries, not by the payer. Three levers move it far more than price does: conversion rate (halve the
free-per-Pro ratio and contribution roughly doubles), free-tier AI usage (§2 already says *"if real usage
runs above ~2 generations/day for free users, lower the free allowance to 2 before raising the price"* —
that sentence is now load-bearing), and annual billing (§7.1). Egress, once measured, can only push it
down.

**Do not treat the number as a plan.** It omits the two unmeasured inputs above, assumes every card is
an EEA standard card, and assumes 5% conversion, which is an aspiration rather than an observation.

## 8. Open questions""")
open(p,"w").write(s)
print("ok")
PY

`main` is `3d71305`, tree clean, nothing in flight. Here's what's left and what I'd do.

## Build next: #12a wear-confirmation

It's the only thing in the queue that's fully unblocked, and yesterday's break-even work made it more important, not less. Your contribution per Pro came out at **~€0.28**, dominated by free users — and the lever that moves that is conversion, which depends on `wear_logs` having enough data to make Pro's analytics worth buying in month three. This is now the *only* mechanism nudging people to log a wear, since push is parked.

It needs one decision from you first, which I flagged in the plan: **what a backdrop tap does.** My recommendation is that it closes for the session without setting `askedOn`, so a mis-tap doesn't silently consume the day's question.

## Then, in order

| | | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **#13** `item-signals-in-generator` | ready | Where `HOT_MATERIALS` finally dies and warmth reads material × texture. Self-contained. |
| **#10** `wear-stats` | **blocked** | Needs the gap-analysis design decision — *"unlocks 14 new outfits"* is a simulation, not a query. Also needs the Pro gate added; the plan predates the entitlements seam. |
| **#14** `route-url-audit` | runs last | By design — touching routes before the screens exist means doing it twice. |
| **#16** full design audit | after all of the above | `impeccable` + `design-taste-frontend`, at phone width. |

## Two non-code items the break-even work surfaced

These aren't in any plan, and one is time-sensitive:

**Measure Supabase egress.** It's the single unmeasured input that can only push contribution *down*, and it's cheap to find out — the Supabase dashboard reports it. Worth doing before you trust any model.

**⚠️ Open-Meteo's commercial licence.** Not optional the day Pro is charged for, and weather sits on the critical path of every generate. This is the only item on the list with legal rather than engineering consequences, so it wants a decision before billing exists — not after.

Neither blocks #12a.

## My recommendation

Start **#12a** now, and answer the backdrop question when I get to Task 3. In parallel, when you're next in the Supabase dashboard, grab the egress number and I'll fold it into `MONETISATION.md`.

Replaces the twice-rejected **"Auto-log worn looks"** toggle with the honest version: after 18:00 local, if a look was *opened* today and nothing was logged, ask once — **Yes** or **No**.

## Why not auto-log

Opening a look is not wearing it. `wear_logs` is the foundation of cost-per-wear, streaks, most-worn, gathering-dust and gap analysis — i.e. of everything Pro sells. Logging views as wears inflates all of it permanently, with **no way afterwards to tell a fabricated wear from a real one**. `MONETISATION.md` §1: *"they pay for it in month three, once the data is theirs."* A poisoned month three is not worth saving one tap.

It needs no push, so unlike the daily fit reminder it is buildable today.

## The two rules that decide whether this helps or harms

Both were stated by the user and are enforced by tests, not by prose.

1. **Yes and No carry exactly equal weight.** They are styled from one shared string, and a test asserts the two class lists are equal — two lists that merely look alike are two things that can drift. There is no Skip, Not now or close: a lone "Yes" with a dismiss ✕ gets tapped to clear the sheet, and the data inflates anyway. The easiest escape becomes the default answer, and here the default would be a lie.
2. **It asks only about looks actually opened**, most recent first. Nothing recorded an open before this, which is the one schema change: `outfits.viewed_at`.

The backdrop dismisses **without recording anything**, so the sheet is not a trap and a mis-tap does not silently consume the day's only chance to log the wear.

## Notable decisions

- **`viewed_at` is stamped from the CLIENT on mount**, never in the route's render. Mutating during render is a side effect React may run twice, and it would fire for a prefetch the user never looked at — putting looks into the confirmation that were never on screen.
- **Yes goes through `toggleWear`, never a second insert path.** `wear_logs_unique_day` is what guarantees one row per outfit per day, and every wear count in the product is a count of those rows.
- **`wearAskedOn` is written BEFORE the wear write.** If the write fails the user is not re-asked tonight: a missed log beats a sheet that reappears until they answer the way it wants.
- **Mounted on `/generate`**, not the shell — it is the home tab and where a returning user lands, while the shell would fire it mid-capture and mid-edit.
- **`localHourFor` pins `hourCycle: "h23"`** because some locales render midnight as "24", which never compares below the evening threshold and would ask the question at 00:00.

## One bug found while verifying

**"Yes" could delete the wear it had just confirmed.** `answerWearConfirmation` called `toggleWear`, and that is a *toggle* — against an outfit already logged today it removes the row. Unreachable through the sheet, because `shouldAsk` refuses to ask once a wear exists (verified live: no sheet, and the look shows its WORN TODAY badge). - **Colours are a constrained vocabulary of 42**, `z.enum` over `COLOR_NAMES`. Neutral vs accent drives
  `colorHarmonyScore`, which gives one accent free — so menswear foundations (navy, denim, camel, khaki,
  chocolate, brown, taupe…) count as neutral.
- **Auto-logging wears was rejected twice.** Opening a look is not wearing it; `wear_logs` is the
  foundation of everything Pro sells. The evening confirmation asks instead — Yes/No equally weighted,
  no third way out.
- **Notifications are DEFERRED** (`plans/scoping/2026-08-11-notifications.md`). The gate is **installs,
  not a native app**: iOS 16.4+ delivers push to home-screen PWAs.
- **A location change rebuilds today's drop, free.** Intent decides, not distance.

Branch → PR → CI `verify` green → merge; `main` is protected by a ruleset with **no bypass actors**, so
`gh pr merge --admin` does NOT work — the ruleset must be disabled and re-enabled, or a bypass actor
added. TDD every change, and **measure before fixing**. **Drive the real app before calling UI work
done** — PRs #21, #23, #28, #29, #30 and #31 each shipped a bug that green tests could not see.
No AI attribution anywhere ([[no-ai-attribution]]). Small scoped plans
([[prefer-multiple-scoped-plans]]), future-proof at forks ([[prefer-future-proof-architecture]]),
and **ask before coding on open decisions** ([[ask-before-coding-on-open-decisions]]).

See [[fitcheck-project]], [[daily-drop-model]], [[end-of-build-design-audit]], [[future-occasion-learner]].
